that this phase must consolidate or retire**, plus two written-but-
unexecuted hardening plans (SQL-side filters; inbound pipeline). This phase
grooms all of that against the researched semantics and completes the

**What it covers.**

- **Conversation model**: one canonical thread with typed parts (customer
  message / staff reply / internal note / system event — notes structurally
  never deliverable), status lifecycle (decide Front-lightweight
  open/snoozed/closed vs Zendesk-full at grooming; snooze-with-timer and
  reopen-on-reply either way).
- **Collision detection that blocks send** on mid-compose updates (Help
  Scout semantics) — the highest-ROI delta over a shared mailbox.
- **Assignment**: individual + team, manual, round-robin, and rules
  conditioned on CRM party data (donor tier, missionary link, content, wait
  time); an explicit unassigned queue. Launch routing is a bounded coded
  policy, not a second tenant-authored automation engine.
- **CRM linking**: auto-match sender → party on exact email;
  suggest-and-confirm for unknown senders (never HubSpot-style auto-create
  junk); conversations on the person timeline via the Phase 6 emit-hook with
  the dedupe rule (support replies must not double-write timeline events).
- **Inbound ingestion**: forwarding-based + BYO-domain (MX/inbound routes)
  with verification; RFC-2822 threading (In-Reply-To/References) +
  unguessable plus-address tokens as fallback; quoted-reply stripping;
  attachment limits. The provider spike qualifies Resend Inbound against the
  mandatory contract first. Other providers remain contingency research only
  if Resend cannot satisfy a mandatory inbound capability; Phase 26 does not
  ship a multi-provider mail adapter.
- **The safety layer ships before real domains open**: suspended/quarantine
  review queue (never silently drop), Auto-Submitted/Precedence:bulk
  detection, per-sender loop rate limits (Zendesk's 20/hr-suspend, 40/hr-
  reject budget), DMARC-failure and own-address-loop guards.
- **Outbound failure states on the conversation** (pending → retrying →
  undelivered/bounced) from the Resend webhooks + Phase 6 monotonic machine.
- **SLA machinery** (schema exists): first-reply/next-reply/resolution
  against business-hours calendars — groom whether small missions teams need
  enforcement UI at launch or reporting suffices.
- **Macros/canned responses** through the Phase 17 variable allow-list.

**Boundaries & guardrails.** Support Hub owns support work — not CRM truth,
provider mail truth, message-template truth, or member-care private truth
(care-classified subjects route to Phase 38 surfaces, not the general inbox).
Phase 17 owns and prepares governed replies; Phase 6 dispatches and records them.
Existing `support_automation_rules` remain inert versioned data until Phase 34
becomes the sole configurable trigger/condition/action vocabulary and
adopts or migrates them; Phase 26 does not forward-gate on Phase 34 or ship a
parallel builder.

**Open questions for grooming.** Whether donors/missionaries get a "my
messages" portal view (rides Phase 6 projections) or the hub stays
staff-only; conversation merge/split at launch; retention/redaction class
for message bodies + attachments (Phase 6 redact-not-delete interplay);

## Decision

Phase 26 provides ordinary email continuation with the tenant's support team.
Donors, missionaries, church representatives and other legitimate requesters can
ask for help and read and reply to the ordinary answer without creating an Asym
account, signing in, opening a portal, completing a CRM link, entering a ticket
number, or passing through mandatory self-service. Qualified website/portal Help
entry points retain permitted context. Phase 26 includes no requester My messages
archive. The reply identifies the tenant and uses its governed, activated and
monitored return route.

Email participation, a matched address, a Party link, a thread reference and a
support assignment do not grant identity, representation, protected-record access
or authority to change money. Protected disclosures and consequential actions use
the existing owner's minimally sufficient qualified flow, which may support a
guest, and preserve context. Ordinary conversation does not need that verification
merely because a later action might. Support resolution never proves an owner
action completed.

Staff work in one canonical support conversation with accurate actor attribution,
explicit recipients, structurally private notes, recoverable drafts, safe concurrent
reply decisions and truthful delivery/recovery evidence. Support reads permitted
CRM context and invokes owner commands; it creates no second CRM, synchronization

evidence.heading: ### D3-R01 — Four mutually exclusive meanings and mixed waits
evidence.text:
### D3-R01 — Four mutually exclusive meanings and mixed waits

“A conversation has exactly one authoritative current work meaning. Open means Support currently owes a substantive next step or a due review/follow-up, including reviewing new input. Waiting for requester means requested information/action from admitted people seeking support is the remaining active blocker. Waiting on our side means a necessary input already sought from a colleague, owning-domain process or outside party is outstanding and Support retains responsibility for obtaining it. Resolved is an explicit completion of the Support obligation, not simply read, out of the inbox or no immediate response needed.”

“If Support currently owes a substantive next step or a due review/follow-up, use Open. Merely being able to send an optional progress update does not end a genuine wait. Otherwise, if an active our-side blocker remains, use Waiting on our side, including mixed requester/our-side waits. Use Waiting for requester only when the remaining active blocker is requester-side. Preserve additional context in existing notes or permitted owner references; do not introduce a fifth Mixed status, mandatory blocker taxonomy or dependency graph. Hypothetical future tasks are not active blockers. An inability to determine the correct wait calls for staff review, not inferred resolution or a fifth normal state.”

evidence.heading: ### D3-R08 — New input, failures and resolution eligibility
evidence.text:
### D3-R08 — New input, failures and resolution eligibility

“A first-time admitted relevant human reply returns the conversation to Open for review and invalidates its obsolete deferral, even if the sender's timestamp predates a prior resolution. Durable intake/effect identity prevents duplicate delivery from reopening work again. Automated, quarantined, malicious, unrelated or already-applied intake is not a human work transition. A newly available result for the current awaited authorized owner action also creates review work; stale/superseded references do not blindly change status.”

“Fresh adverse evidence requiring staff investigation—such as a relevant unresolved delivery failure or ambiguous outcome—creates Open review work through the same causal boundary, including after a prior resolution. Preserve the prior resolution as history; this does not declare it dishonest retrospectively. Do not reopen for every duplicate callback or an already-reviewed/provably superseded result. When relevance cannot safely be established, retain visible qualified review work rather than silently discard the evidence. Provider/member evidence remains under D1/D2.”

“Resolve is deliberate and cannot hide a known outstanding Support obligation, promised follow-up or required unreviewed recovery action. It does not certify receipt/read status or complete a giving/CRM/document/care action. Pending automated delivery remains separately visible and recoverable; a later failure may create new review work. No required donor courtesy acknowledgement is added after an otherwise complete answer. Reading, adding a note or completing an owner UI is never implicit resolution.”

No arbitrary no-response timeout, irreversible Closed stage, automatic closure email, SLA pause or default Send-and-resolve behavior is selected by D3. An explicit future Send-and-status convenience must expose both effects and satisfy the same approval, transaction and recovery contracts. User-selected work intent must not be replaced by text classification or AI guessing.

evidence.heading: ### D5-R01 — Meaning and proportionate eligibility
evidence.text:
### D5-R01 — Meaning and proportionate eligibility

“No response is the reason staff deliberately ended further Support follow-up because clearly requested needed input remains absent. It is not a count of human messages or proof of refusal, neglect, delivery, satisfaction or an achieved business outcome. Identify the current remaining need using existing authorized conversation context and references to the relevant request and latest reviewed input; do not add a generic blocker graph or require a long new form.”

“New relevant partial information or an acknowledgement first creates D3 review and invalidates an older ending approval. After review, staff may retain a clearly still-unanswered portion of the existing request as the basis for a later ending; another chaser email is not mandatory merely to requalify it. If the required information has arrived, the requester explicitly declined or cannot supply it, withdrew the request, or asked staff a new clarification question, do not silently treat that response as the same no-response basis. Handle the actual current work. ‘No further response’ may explain the situation in prose, but does not create a second disposition.”

“Use the same four D3 work meanings. Eligibility follows current reviewed obligations, not only the current Waiting for requester label: due reminders may already have made the conversation Open. An active our-side Support obligation prevents this ending; the mere existence of an unrelated linked owner-domain process does not. Ordinary completion still needs no requester courtesy acknowledgement after an otherwise complete answer.”

evidence.heading: ### D5-R03 — Commitments and domain authority
evidence.text:
### D5-R03 — Commitments and domain authority

“An ending cannot waive a known required Support action, promise, currently relevant owner obligation that Support must follow through on, or required unreviewed recovery. Use the existing owner-authorized status/action/reference contracts for known guards. Check necessary owner evidence under current permissions; unavailable required evidence is not success. Explain a blocked or unavailable review without exposing restricted details.”

“Do not scan every CRM relationship or pretend software can prove the meaning of every free-text promise. Server-enforced known facts and accountable human review serve different roles. No mandatory checkbox substitutes for owner authorization, and no new generic task/claim/approval engine is required. Authorized correction remains possible without claiming that audit alone prevents deliberate misuse.”

“Support owns its work status, ending record and conversation. CRM owns Parties and relationships; giving, receipts/documents, recurring gifts, refunds and member-care retain their own permissions, validation, approval, completion and audit. End follow-up does not cancel or dismiss those owner records. A support assignment, requester link or conversation membership never grants access to them. Care-classified content retains its Phase 38 boundary; No response is not a way to move it into the general inbox.”

evidence.heading: ### D10-R24 — Predictable subject, priority, labels and service history
evidence.text:
### D10-R24 — Predictable subject, priority, labels and service history

“Keep the explicitly reviewed continuing conversation's current staff subject. Original email subjects and headers remain unchanged; staff naming does not rewrite external threads. The proposed resulting priority is the highest priority of the TWO CURRENT work components, not every dormant original row. An explicit authorized priority change may choose another valid value in the review. Undo previews both current resulting priorities, using the current combined priority as a suggestion rather than restoring historical source values.”

“Existing label memberships remain on original conversation endpoints. The combined view is their permitted deduplicated union; a new label Add anchors to the continuing origin and is unchanged if already effective. Combined Remove targets exact current contributors; current Undo/merge separation preserves later edits and original membership. This reuses the existing label vocabulary and the same source-aware command discipline as D9 links, not another taxonomy. Merely composing or separating effective labels fires no synthetic label-added/removed email or automation.”

“Keep original created/first-message/SLA timestamps and policy evidence. Current first/last-message displays derive from actual permitted source occurrences and are labeled as message times, not new case creation or SLA eligibility. Merge/Undo cannot restart a service clock, erase a prior breach, inherit a policy from the latest update or silently discard an active service obligation. The chosen Phase 26 SLA/reporting scope remains its separate grooming decision; whichever owner policy is activated must qualify merge/separation using retained source evidence before enforcement or reporting ships.”

evidence.heading: ### D10-R01 — Narrow purpose and explicit eligibility
evidence.text:
### D10-R01 — Narrow purpose and explicit eligibility

“Merge is an explicit staff conclusion that two current Support work components represent the same request. The launch command joins one reviewed pair of current roots in the same tenant and current inbox. Current source classification and permissions must permit the resulting work. Use the existing authorized inbox Move first when appropriate; Merge never performs a hidden cross-inbox move. Different channels, member-care boundaries or incompatible independent obligations are not admitted merely because the worker can see both.”

“No AI/similarity auto-merge, bulk merge, arbitrary field-merging wizard or required CRM Party identity is added. Same-address/subject/reference ambiguity is resolved under D1, not used as semantic merge authority. Truly separate requests remain separate. General topic splitting is not part of this decision; undoing a mistaken merge is.”

evidence.heading: ### D10-R02 — Original evidence and a reversible handling relationship
evidence.text:
### D10-R02 — Original evidence and a reversible handling relationship

“Keep each original conversation ID, its source messages, original endpoints/headers/times, attachment custody, source business references and history stable. Each original conversation belongs to exactly one current handling component. Its current root is the continuing conversation; there is no second copied ticket or mutable transcript store.”

“Represent active merges as a narrow rooted forest: a source root has at most one active parent; a root has no active parent; cycles and self-merge are forbidden. Merge only current distinct roots, adding one operation-owned active edge from the source root to the explicitly chosen continuing root. Ended edges remain audit evidence. A materialized root lookup is a derived acceleration, not write authority.”

“An old URL is resolved visibly through current handling before a new action is reviewed. Cached root IDs or permanent redirects cannot freeze that relationship after Undo; navigation requalifies current topology and access. Selecting an original already in the same component reports Already combined; it does not create another edge. Re-merging after Undo creates a new edge/generation and receipt. Original source identity and current handling identity remain distinct in every API and projection.”

evidence.heading: ### D10-R04 — Current authorization without access expansion
evidence.text:
### D10-R04 — Current authorization without access expansion

“A merge or Undo requires current Support capability and resource authority for the complete affected components and exact resulting work/assignment/reminder actions. Current combined handling access is qualified across constituent source conversation protection; each message, attachment, note, CRM record and field keeps its own stricter owner floor. Ability to view two items once is not authority to widen either item's audience.”

“Reuse Phase 12's PDP and resource-purpose contracts. No union ACL, merged-reader role, new tenant-role fallback or caller-supplied actor is introduced. Browser, RPC/view, service-role/NHI, jobs, exports and cache paths enforce the same boundaries. Same inbox is a scope simplification, not authorization proof.”

“Later source permission/classification loss takes effect immediately without waiting for merge repair or portfolio enumeration. Full combined reads/actions fail safely where no longer permitted; qualified owners may correct/separate the affected work. A narrower original-source inspection must not reveal inaccessible root/member names, counts, excerpts or topology. Owner-safe denial and operational recovery cannot become a hidden-content leak.”

evidence.heading: ### D10-R07 — Source-aware future email and correlation
evidence.text:
### D10-R07 — Source-aware future email and correlation

“Every admitted message/recovery effect retains its immutable source identity. Resolve its original thread/source from qualified owner correlation, then resolve current handling atomically with the D3 effect. If input wins before Undo, the Undo preview includes it; if Undo wins, the input creates work in the resulting current component. Replayed original effects do not open both sides.”

“Preserve original Message-ID, In-Reply-To, References and approved reply-route provenance. A reply to either original conversation continues in the root while merged and follows its original current component after separation. Conflicting or insufficient original-source evidence remains in the existing durable thread/route-review path; even references resolving to the same current root must not erase ambiguity needed for later correction. No arbitrary first match or current-root guess replaces source evidence.”

“Unrelated new email without qualified thread evidence remains new serviceable intake. A past merge does not authorize sender/subject auto-adoption. Resend transports and reports mail facts; Support owns current handling. The donor's external mailbox may retain two old threads. No promise is made to rewrite external mailbox history.”

evidence.heading: ### D10-R09 — One work outcome without manufactured completion
evidence.text:
### D10-R09 — One work outcome without manufactured completion

“Merge presents one resulting current D3 work plan. Open dominates when any source owes action or required review; matching waits may retain that meaning; mixed blocking waits use Waiting on our side when no immediate action is owed, as D3 already requires. Both legitimately complete sources may remain Resolved. Staff can select another currently valid plan only through the same explicit D3 authority and obligation checks.”

“The absorbed source becomes handled in the continuing conversation, not a newly successful resolution or No response ending. Preserve its historical work episodes and facts; no hidden legacy Resolved write may trigger closure mail, success reporting or D5 automation. New work from either original source remains visible. Merge cannot swallow an outstanding Support promise, required recovery or unreviewed owner outcome associated with a financial action. An independent owner process retains its own state and need not keep Support work Open.”

evidence.heading: ### D19-R01 — Scope and one accountable operating model
evidence.text:
### D19-R01 — Scope and one accountable operating model

Support Hub owns the ordinary business-review decision for accepted input that is already bound to a trustworthy tenant and a qualified review scope. Designate reviewers per responsible inbox, backed by tenant oversight; one eligible team may cover multiple or all inboxes. Reuse Core membership, teams, authorization, attention and durable work capabilities after qualifying them for this purpose. Do not create a new omnipotent reviewer role, a second help desk, CRM, classification engine or tenant workflow builder.

evidence.heading: ### D19-R05 — Quiet, source-authorized queue
evidence.text:
### D19-R05 — Quiet, source-authorized queue

Show **Needs review** within Support Hub and as an inbox-scoped view for eligible staff. Default to items requiring a business decision; keep technical recovery visibly separate as **Processing issues** for qualified operators. List authorized sender/address, subject or safe fallback, responsible inbox, plain reason, received age and content expiry. No body snippets by default. An informational header says: “Incoming email held before it enters Support work.” It does not call every item spam or a ticket. Include **To review**, **Processing**, and **History** views; history filters distinguish Released, Dismissed and Expired. Counts, search matches, pagination and empty states are authorized at source, including metadata. “No messages need a decision” requires successful loading of the stated scope and must not conceal authorized pending releases. Unknown or partial scope is explicit without leaking concealed records. Processing here means pending release only; Processing issues remains the qualified technical-recovery view. They reference the same source rather than duplicate it.

evidence.heading: ### D19-R10 — Dismissal and correction
evidence.text:
### D19-R10 — Dismissal and correction

**Dismiss** means “Keep this message out of Support work.” It records one typed reason and removes the item from To review; it neither blocks future mail nor deletes a CRM contact or immediately destroys content. Show “Recoverable until [exact original deadline]” and a persistent **Return to review** action in History while current authority and content lifetime permit. A transient Undo can invoke that same command, but is never the only recovery route. Returning to review does not release, renew content retention or clear safety gates. At expiry the action becomes unavailable with an honest explanation; no background lag extends the recovery promise. Preserve Dismissed as the historical decision and Content expired as current availability; expiry does not rewrite who decided or imply a missed business review.

evidence.heading: ### D19-R18 — Correct a mistaken release truthfully
evidence.text:
### D19-R18 — Correct a mistaken release truthfully

Before canonical admission commits, a qualified **Cancel release** may stop a pending release through the same current source guard. If admission has committed or cannot yet be reconciled, the UI must not promise Undo or deletion: reconcile first, then offer the authorized conversation/source correction path. Existing D9/D10/D16 owner commands handle wrong links, actual duplicates or unsafe admitted content; stop unsafe pending effects through their actual owner. Never unsend mail, erase valid staff work, delete CRM facts or make a delivered message disappear to simulate reversal. Preserve original review and correction evidence. A later security restriction always applies even if the earlier decision was legitimate.

evidence.heading: ### D19-R23 — Email Studio, Resend and attention
evidence.text:
### D19-R23 — Email Studio, Resend and attention

Review UI is not an email composer. Keep D18's ratified Email Studio ownership of reusable content and prepared human replies, and D13's separate qualified **Support request received** template. Intake Release/Dismiss/Retry use neither a canned reply nor an ad hoc email template. Resend remains the qualified receiving provider; tenant/provider authority must be proven before fetch/replay, and Phase 6 remains the only external dispatch/evidence owner. Raw provider URLs and connection secrets stay server-side.

Use the shared in-product attention capability for coverage failure, aged unresolved review and expiring unresolved content; qualify a bounded source meaning and the existing source-actionable presentation policy before enabling it. Group by tenant/inbox/condition and reauthorize at display. Read/archive is not source completion. Default reviewer attention is in-product with no per-message email, external sender notification, push/body digest or dedicated notification engine. Any later authorized email channel must use an exact Email Studio meaning/template plus P6/tenant Resend; it cannot be assembled by a queue worker or extend source lifetime.

evidence.heading: ### D19-R25 — Reuse qualified capabilities and retire conflicting paths
evidence.text:
### D19-R25 — Reuse qualified capabilities and retire conflicting paths

Extend the canonical intake/source workflow, guarded API boundary, existing team/permission system, source-backed CRM read model, Email Studio/P6 and records/asset owners. Requalify rather than blindly reuse current retry, route-resume, first-match threading, audit or broad staff endpoints. Preserve actual provider evidence and legacy input identity while consolidating the older parallel Support path. The existing future-route command cannot be relabeled single-message release. Leave Phase 34 as the sole configurable rule-engine owner. No queue-specific CRM, new sender registry, local template/compiler, custom security scanner or generic review/approval platform is introduced.

evidence.heading: ### D19-R30 — Deliberately limited scope
evidence.text:
### D19-R30 — Deliberately limited scope

The complete launch journey is configure coverage, inspect, decide, correct, recover and oversee. It does not add a requester quarantine portal, automatic trust learning, AI release decisions, reply-from-quarantine, mass allowlists, mandatory two-person review, routine legal approval, mailbox synchronization, enterprise security console or another workflow platform. A person may receive review authority and remain unable to read a restricted conversation or CRM record. International names/addresses remain intact; translated labels and exact local dates support comprehension without transforming identifier equality or pausing server clocks.

## Full adversarial category review

Severity describes the plausible impact without the amendment. Likelihood is qualitative engineering judgment about implementation/operation exposure, not measured ministry incidence. The evidence register distinguishes inspected facts, external documentation, inference and product judgment. Each finding changes or narrows A as specified; none requires abandoning designated responsibility.

evidence.heading: ### D28-R04 Eligibility is source-owned
evidence.text:
### D28-R04 Eligibility is source-owned

A genuine ordinary Resolved completion can create a generation-bound candidate while the policy and inbox are enabled. At maturity, current source facts must still show completed ordinary work, an admitted external human request, qualified actual human email correspondence with that recipient, and a currently qualified recipient/send basis. A known accepted human reply establishes only transport evidence, not human receipt or satisfaction. Unresolved submission, missing authority, No response endings, spam/auto-only intake, drafts, internal-note-only work, restricted care content, suppressed endpoints and manual-only work lacking actual qualified email do not establish eligibility. A caller-supplied closure intent is not completion evidence: still-owed Support commitments and actionable unreviewed recovery block it under the existing owner rules. No arbitrary minimum message count or AI judgment substitutes for these facts. Exclusions and the email-only population limit are reported honestly.

evidence.heading: ### D28-R11 Merge, Undo and historical conservation
evidence.text:
### D28-R11 Merge, Undo and historical conservation

Keep immutable original conversation/opportunity/effect identities. Before sampling and submission, serialize against current D10 topology. If multiple unsampled candidates belong to one current component, select one neutrally eligible representative by earliest genuine completion instant then stable original ID and admit only its draw. Any prior component opportunity, including Not selected, prevents another original supplying a new chance. Record an immutable linked-suppression disposition for each otherwise eligible losing original, referencing that original opportunity without a fresh draw; Undo cannot revive it. Two independently committed pre-merge draws remain historical facts. A component with a prior possible/submitted invitation suppresses pending duplicates. If independent pending invitations merge, retain one deterministically by earliest genuine completion instant then original stable ID and suppress others. Two invitations submitted before their conversations merged remain two historical facts; no history rewrite or recall fiction. Undo alone creates no invitation, restores no cancelled generation and grants no new draw. CRM Party merging is distinct from Support merging and cannot create or transfer sampling authority.

evidence.heading: ### D28-R24 Honest measurement
evidence.text:
### D28-R24 Honest measurement

Report completion candidates/basic exclusions, matured eligible opportunities, selected/not selected, post-selection suppression reasons, submission-may-have-begun, accepted/unknown/failed/delivered evidence and submitted responses as distinct units. Invitation cohort dates are explicit; response-date browsing is distinct from cohort conversion. Preserve original effect counts after merges and show currently permitted original inbox/cohort provenance. Define issued as distinct invitation effects whose submission may have begun. Response fraction is unique responded-issued invitations divided by that same issued cohort, including indeterminate submissions; it never divides all responses only by provider-confirmed acceptances. Present counts and distribution of the three choices; if showing satisfied-share, define Satisfied / all non-excluded submitted ratings and show its denominator. No response is not positive or negative. Sampling is random among qualified opportunities, not all donors or unique people; frequency/eligibility exclusions and voluntary response mean no representativeness or margin-of-error claim. Do not offer employee leaderboards or cross-vendor benchmark comparison.

# ADR-0016: Selective permanent source redaction

**Status: Fully founder-ratified, 11 September 2026.** The founder selected A—Selective permanent redaction and requested proportionate UX, US legal research and the complete adversarial review. D1–D15 remain fully ratified. This is local grooming authority, not a formal specification or implementation.

## Decision and tradeoff

Accept A with the complete fully ratified D16-R01–R24, P01–P40, all23 category findings, complete UX/evidence and six operational controls. Authorized staff deliberately select exact content in one original message and whole selected files, review the safe remainder, and commit once. Preserve useful unselected content and permitted body-free communication facts. Whole-body removal is the strongest simpler fallback; retained revealable masking adds custody risk and is not the ordinary correction model. No completed-redaction Undo or revealable Support archive.

Support owns original source correction. Current source restrictions govern every active representation, including inbound parsed/MIME, alternate bodies, attachments, drafts, P6/P17 material, search, CRM and exports. A hidden span is insufficient. Keep current restriction, durable content-free operation receipt and owner cleanup evidence distinct. Real preservation restrictions use qualified custody; unknown checks never authorize disposal. Provider/backup cleanup has actual owner deadlines/evidence and no external recall promise. Corrected completion evidence may reopen cleanup without restoring source content.

CRM and other business domains remain authoritative for their own facts and permissions; linking, assignment or correction capability grants no additional access. D10 merge/Undo and D12 citations resolve current sanitized originals. D14 metrics, work and D15 following remain truthful and quiet. P6 dispatching is the send boundary; privacy stops prohibit further payload attempts, and ADR0032 sealed envelopes cannot be split/rerendered/rekeyed. Fresh review cannot replace accepted or indeterminate sends. Preserve the existing prepared-material purge deadline.

## Consequences and required proof

The ordinary UI is a message action, exact selection, after-state preview, one meaningful confirmation and a persistent neutral marker. Precise selection needs keyboard/AT/touch support; a whole-body accessibility substitute is insufficient. No automatic scanner, binary editor, universal retention schedule, compliance platform, second CRM or routine correction email is selected. US applicability depends on actual entity/role/jurisdiction/data and records duties; redaction is not complete legal compliance, privacy-request fulfillment or incident response.

Current source exposes duplicate body representations, generic staff DML/audit and unqualified cache/selection seams. The three pure-source probe observations falsify reuse of current text extraction as a precise selection mapper; they are not a deployed vulnerability or D16 implementation test. Require grants/RLS/service parity, exact original relations, source-gated private files, legacy URL qualification, owner inventory, source/hold/send races, restoration barriers and compatible activation before Live use. No unknown current delivery path can be enabled merely by labelling containment incomplete.

# ADR-0017: Automatic Support content expiry

**Status: Fully founder-ratified, 11 September 2026.** The founder selected A—Automatically expire content after Support work ends and requested full CRM/database, policy UX, modern-practice research and adversarial review. D1–D16 remain fully ratified. This is local grooming authority, not a formal specification or running implementation.

## Decision and tradeoff

Accept A with the complete fully ratified D17-R01–R26, P01–P43, all 23 category findings, full policy/CRM UX, exact kept/expired/independently owned data inventory, research qualifications, adopted independent corrections and seven operational controls. Use one finite tenant default for ordinary Support bodies and files, explicitly reviewed and activated with existing-plus-future unexpired scope. No universal numeric default, per-inbox/attachment override hierarchy, Never switch or routine per-item approval. B's review-first default creates recurring work; C's individual-age expiry can fragment active context.

Base ordinary inactivity on genuine source-purpose completion and first durable native human-content admission, not mutable status/update fields or provider callback acceptance. All Support-owned content through the expired frontier, including automatic/system bodies, enters disposal; only the qualified human subset renews the clock. Status-only cycling does not renew age.
